item.title: Trump on Suspected Russia Plague: In Very Deep Discussions
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Lauren French, Senate Majority PAC senior advisor, says the PAC is making spending decisions week by week after pulling out of North Carolina and is looking closely at races in Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi. Gen. Charles Wald, USAF Retired, says threats against US military bases are not unusual and says the departure of B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford is being depicted “a little bit out of context.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anwar Set to Boost Spending in 2027 Budget as Election Speculation Grows
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is expected to tackle rising living costs in potentially his government’s last budget before he calls national elections.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar

item.title: Wald Says RAF Fairford B-1 Move Is Depicted Out of Context
item.description: Gen. Charles Wald, USAF Retired, says threats against US military bases are not unusual and says the departure of B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford is being depicted “a little bit out of context.” Wald says moving the bombers was a smart precaution and says the growing drone threat is getting significant attention from the US military. Wald says the US can learn from the creativity Ukraine has demonstrated in its use of drones during the war. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: French: We’re Going to Win Michigan, New Hampshire and Maine
item.description: Lauren French, Senate Majority PAC senior advisor, says the PAC is making spending decisions week by week after pulling out of North Carolina and is looking closely at races in Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi. French says Democrats may not be able to match Republican spending, but says Democratic candidates are outraising Republicans. French says that the October surprise will be if polling has been accurate or not and believes that Democrats will win Michigan, New Hampshire and Maine. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: AI Bulls Take The Lead (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Just a week ahead of the earnings season, the S&P 500 headed toward its first record close since August. Strong corporate earnings, enthusiasm around the artificial intelligence trade and a US economy that has so far avoided a significant slowdown have fueled a roughly 14% advance in the S&P 500 this year. The rally is getting additional support from lower oil prices, which have helped temper concerns about rising consumer costs.
On today's episode:
Eric Weiner, Bloomberg News Senior Editor for Equities Sastry Durvasula, Chief Operating Officer at TIAA Laura Rippy, Managing Partner at Alumni Ventures Eric So, Author of 'The Collision' & Professor of Economics at MIT Sloan School of Management (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kosovo Averts Early Elections as Lawmakers Back New President
item.description: Kosovo averted a snap vote as political parties reached a last-minute agreement to limit the powers of a war crimes court and elect Justina Shiroka-Pula as president.
item.dc:creator: Gresa Kraja

item.title: Trump Resists Deeper US Role in Saudi Arabia-Houthi Conflict
item.description: The Trump administration is reluctant to get more involved in Saudi Arabia’s offensive against the Houthis and has tried to restrain Riyadh from sparking a major new conflict in Yemen, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan, Courtney McBride and Fiona MacDonald

item.title: S&P 500 Hits Record High as Big Tech Leads
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are UBS Alignment Partners Managing Director, Wealth Management Alli McCartney, Wedbush Securities Senior VP, Equity Research Alicia Reese, ZScaler CEO, Chairman, & Founder Jay Chaudhry, BlackRock Head of US Wealth & Retirement Business Jaime Magyera, Kayne Anderson Rudnick Portfolio Manager, Senior Research Analyst Julie Biel, Kearney Grocery & Retail, Americas Lead Katherine Black, Hamilton Lane Co-Head of Real Estate Elizabeth Bell, Union Square Advisors President & Co-Founder Ted Smith, Dimensional Fund Advisors Portfolio Management Deputy Head, North America Joel Schneider, & Churchill Asset Management CEO Ken Kencel. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Is Becoming More of a Reserve Currency, Taleb Says
item.description: Nassim Taleb, author of “The Black Swan” and distinguished scientist at Universa Investments, says gold is becoming more of a reserve currency, because the US dollar is not as reliable as it once was. He speaks at the Greenwich Economic Forum. (Courtesy Greenwich Economic Forum) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He Has Call Scheduled Soon With Putin on Plague
item.description: President Donald Trump said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a suspected plague case, amid growing global health concerns over the incident.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse, Rachel Cohrs Zhang, Eric Martin and Jason Gale

item.title: Red Diesel Move Sows Confusion for Truck Stops, Fuel Sellers
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s order allowing truckers to burn diesel normally reserved for tractors and trawlers won’t do much to immediately lower fuel prices, analysts said.
item.dc:creator: Will Kubzansky, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Ari Natter

item.title: Maine Collins-Jackson Debate Highlights Fight for Senate Control
item.description: The 73-year-old Republican incumbent faces one of her biggest tests yet in one of the most competitive races.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Top-Heavy Stock Rally Dares Bonds
item.description: Wall Street traders drove stocks to all-time highs on growing bets that Corporate America will be able to weather the threats from still-elevated energy costs and interest rates. Bloomberg Opinion's John Authers examines the market backdrop. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon talks AI, inflation, and government debt in conversation with Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie. Isabel Guzman, former SBA Administrator and Chair of the Global Risk Advisory Council, discusses their new Reputation Risk Index report. TIAA COO Sastry Durvasula joins to explain the firm's blueprint for implementing AI at scale. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He’s Considering Gas Tax Suspension to Ease Costs
item.description: President Donald Trump said that he is weighing a potential suspension of the federal gas tax, as his administration looks for ways to ease high energy costs ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Brazil Elections: Bolsonaro Secures Key Endorsement for Presidency
item.description: Brazil’s right-wing presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro secured the backing of veteran lawmaker Ronaldo Caiado on Tuesday as he moves to consolidate support from first-round rivals before a tight runoff.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Simone Iglesias

item.title: Four Weeks to Election Day
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the midterm elections. On today's show, Republican Congressman Brad Knott of North Carolina, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Democratic Congressman Joe Morelle of New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Ramps Up Ship Attacks in Hormuz as Oil, Gas Flows Climb
item.description: Iran has increased the pace of attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, just as oil shipments through the world’s most important energy chokepoint approach prewar levels.
item.dc:creator: Alex Longley, Ruth Liao and Grant Smith

item.title: Drone Maker Anduril Pushes Into Subs With Maryland Factory
item.description: Anduril Industries, known for building drones and autonomous aircraft, is investing $3.7 billion to build a massive new shipbuilding facility in Maryland, a move that will enhance the US Navy’s nuclear-powered submarine production.
item.dc:creator: Jen Judson and Courtney McBride

item.title: Midterms 2026: Susan Collins, Troy Jackson Clash Over Costs in Maine Race
item.description: Nazi symbols, sexual assault allegations and months of internal Democratic conflict have churned through the US Senate race in Maine. Yet with the election four weeks away, it’s the explosion in housing costs and record-breaking heating bills that Mainers can’t stop talking about.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ryan

item.title: Indian Opposition Leader Detained After Voter Roll Standoff
item.description: Police in India’s capital, New Delhi, temporarily detained key opposition leader Rahul Gandhi to end an almost nine-hour standoff, during a protest seeking the resignation of the chief election official over a contentious revision of voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Roy and Santosh Kumar
